title: Canonical seek on a tape bank
statement: Let $F$ be a machine format, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $\iota:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ be an injection. There exist a finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, a deterministic Turing machine $R$ with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, entry and exit states in $S$, and a natural number $a$ such that the following holds. For every Boolean input word $x$, natural number $p$, Boolean word $w$ whose base-two value is $p$, and configuration $d$ on input $x$, assume $p\le |x|+1$, the state of $d$ is the entry state, tape $\iota(0)$ contains the buffer representation of $w$ at every integer offset $q$ with $-1\le q\le |w|$, and tape $\iota(1)$ is blank at every integer position. Then for some $t\le a(|w|+d.inputPos.val+p+1)$, the run of $R$ from $d$ has not reached the exit state at any time $u<t$, and at time $t$ it is exactly $d$ with its state changed to the exit state and its input-head position set to $p$.
hypotheses_covered: Injection from two designated indices into the $k$ work-tape indices
